processing_steps.method: vacuum-induction melting (VIM) and casting into Cu molds
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: System modified to enable synthesis of five different alloys in one operation; five Cu molds moved stepwise inside the furnace and successively filled with melt from a 4-kg ingot; after each cast, the remaining melt composition was adjusted by charging Al through an air lock.
10 × 50 × 130 mm^3 blocks were hot rolled into 2 ± 0.1 mm thick and ~500 mm long sheets.
Cut perpendicular to the rolling direction into sets of nine segments with dimensions 2 × 60 × 55 mm^3 for each alloy composition.
Aging was conducted in air at 450 °C, 500 °C, 550 °C, and 600 °C for 0 h, 1 h, and 24 h at each temperature; this sample corresponds to the 450 °C / 24 h condition.
Scales were removed from the surfaces by low-pressure, fine-grit sandblasting after the heat treatments.

structures.overall_structure: Single-phase austenitic (fcc) TWIP/SIMPLEX steel; fully recrystallized microstructure after hot rolling and water quenching

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: All plotted values represent averages of three measurements for every material state.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1; averages of three measurements per material state
characterization_methods.purpose: mechanical screening (yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, total elongation)

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: cross-sectional areas prepared in the plane perpendicular to the rolling direction
characterization_methods.key_findings: No cracks, pores, or macrosegregations in the final materials; as-cast samples had a coarse dendritic microstructure; hot rolling and water quenching gave a fully recrystallized microstructure with ~20 µm grain size and some retained Mn microsegregations.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: performed on the rolling plane of samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm

unmapped_findings: For the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-4Al alloy (an intermediate Al variant), the applied aging treatments have only a weak effect on mechanical data compared with Fe-30Mn-1.2C (weakening/embrittlement) and Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al (strengthening) [b0024].

In the RAP screening, intermediate alloy variants with 2–6 wt.% Al (including this 4Al sample) do not show equivalent mechanical properties to the ~8 wt.% Al variant and show a much smaller influence of aging on tensile behavior [b0025].

In Fig. 4, the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-4Al (blue) points form a low-strength cluster at roughly 460–600 MPa tensile strength with elongation to fracture spanning ~8% to ~55%, aggregating multiple aging conditions (450/500/550/600 °C, 1 h and 24 h); the specific 450 °C/24 h point is not individually identified [figure_004].

Fig. 3 (RAP mechanical-property overview) plots aging curves for 450 °C/1 h, 500 °C/1 h, 550 °C/1 h, 550 °C/24 h, 600 °C/1 h, 600 °C/24 h and as-homogenised, but does not include a 450 °C/24 h curve; therefore no sample-specific YS/UTS/TE/hardness values for the 450 °C/24 h condition are individually reported in the text [figure_003].
